# Configuration reference

Settings come from the environment, then from the config file (`conflu config path`), then from the defaults.

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CONFLUENCE_BASE_URL` | (empty) | Address of the Confluence Cloud site, ending in /wiki. The /wiki is added when it is left out of an atlassian.net address. Example: `https://example.atlassian.net/wiki`. |
| `CONFLUENCE_EMAIL` | (empty) | E-mail address of the Atlassian account that owns the API token. It is shown masked. Example: `user@example.com`. |
| `CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN` | secret | API token of that account. Save it with `conflu setup-token`; it is never printed. |
| `CONFLUENCE_SPACE` | (empty) | Current space; used when --space is left out. Set it with `conflu use KEY`. Example: `ENG`. |
| `CONFLUENCE_CA_BUNDLE` | (empty) | PEM file with certificate authorities to trust in addition to the system store: a private company CA, or a public one that the system store lacks. Empty: the system store alone. Example: `C:/certs/company-ca.pem`. |
| `CONFLUENCE_TLS_STRICT` | `false` | Apply Python's strict X.509 checks on top of the normal verification of the certificate chain and the host name, which always happen. Off by default: the TLS-inspecting proxy of many companies issues certificates that fail them (`Missing Authority Key Identifier`). |
| `CONFLUENCE_INSECURE` | `false` | Do not verify TLS certificates. Only as a temporary diagnostic. |
| `CONFLUENCE_ALLOW_HTTP` | `false` | Allow a plain http:// CONFLUENCE_BASE_URL. The credentials then travel unencrypted, so use it only on an isolated network. Addresses on this computer (localhost) are always allowed. |
| `CONFLUENCE_HIDE_USERS` | `false` | Policy: never print people (names, account ids, e-mail addresses). `--with-users` is then refused. |
| `CONFLUENCE_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` | `10` | Seconds to wait for the connection. |
| `CONFLUENCE_MAX_TIME` | `120` | Seconds to wait for an answer. |
| `CONFLUENCE_RETRY` | `2` | Retries of a read request after a network error or HTTP 429/502/503/504. Writes are never retried. |
| `CONFLUENCE_OUTPUT` | `text` | `json` makes every command that supports it print JSON, as if --json was given. Meant for scripts and agents. Example: `json`. |
| `CONFLUENCE_PROFILE` | (empty) | `agent` is for AI agents: CONFLUENCE_HIDE_USERS=true and CONFLUENCE_OUTPUT=json become the defaults (a value you set yourself still wins), and informational messages stay off standard error. Example: `agent`. |
